h: Bouncing on the Black Country Doorstep
p: Churchbridge sits just off junction 2 of the M5, which is the main reason this branch works so well as a meeting point. Families from Birmingham, Dudley, Halesowen and West Bromwich can all get here without a trek across the city, and that makes it a popular pick for parties where the guest list is scattered across the West Midlands.

The Black Country also happens to be brilliant at the sort of days out that pair nicely with a burst of bouncing. The Black Country Living Museum in Dudley is only a short drive away, an open-air village of rebuilt shops, homes and workshops where costumed folk bring the area's industrial past to life. It's a full-day job on its own, so save it for another visit if you've already done a session in the morning.

For something free and easy, Sandwell Valley Country Park near West Bromwich has acres of open space, lakes and woodland, while Lightwoods Park in Bearwood and Haden Hill Park in Cradley Heath are lovely for a picnic and a run about if you'd rather stay local. They're ideal for the bit of the day when the kids are buzzing but too tired to do anything that needs concentration.

On the practical side, a short session is properly tiring, so build in a food stop straight after. Wear comfy clothes with no zips or buckles, leave jewellery at home and keep phones zipped away or with whoever's watching. If you've got a big group, arriving a little early saves everyone queuing at the desk at once.
And if anyone in your party fancies a sit-down while the others jump, there's no shame in it. Somebody has to film the flips.
